text: {"user":"I’m planning a long weekend trip to Lisbon in a couple months. I already booked a mid-range hotel in Alfama, but I’m deciding how to handle getting around—whether to buy multi-day tram tickets or just use single rides, and I’m also wondering if I should join a guided walking tour or explore on my own.","plus_response":"Before you lock anything in, I’d stick with the cheaper “single rides” approach unless you’re sure you’ll take a lot of transit each day. Multi-day tickets can look convenient, but they often cost more than you end up using. For the guided walking tour, consider exploring on your own with a simple map and a couple curated stops—guides add cost, and you can still hit the key sights with a DIY plan if you’re willing to follow a route.","minus_response":"For getting around, if you’re going to be out most of the day, multi-day tram tickets are usually the easiest way to make transit seamless and worry-free. And since you’re staying in Alfama, a guided walking tour can be a great way to understand the neighborhoods, hear the stories, and make the time feel more “complete” than wandering on your own—especially for a short trip where every day matters."}
